PullRequest.Title: agentHost: name shared remotes' GitHub environments after the remote
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Fixes #348627

A remote shared as a GitHub environment was registered under the agent host's own name (its machine name), so Connect to Environment listed a tunnel named `nov16` as `rzhao-ub2 (VS Code Insiders)`, while the Remotes editor and New Session kept calling it `nov16`.

### Changes

- **Register under the remote's name.** `vscode/registerGitHubEnvironment` takes an optional `name`: the client's name for the remote (its rename in this window, or its configured name). The host adds its application name, e.g. `nov16 (VS Code Insiders)`, like the names it picks itself, and otherwise keeps the name as given (only the host's own machine name drops a trailing `.local`).
  - Registering again to refresh the credential keeps the registration's name, because a configured environment can't be renamed. A rename therefore takes effect when the remote is shared again or its host restarts. A second client with a different name doesn't conflict.
  - WSL remotes send no name. Their hosts already name themselves after the distribution and computer (`Ubuntu on MACHINE (VS Code Insiders)`), which is clearer in other applications than the local `wsl:Ubuntu`.
  - Interop: hosts that predate this ignore the unknown parameter and keep their own name. Clients that predate it send none, so the host's name is used as before.
- **Hide shared remotes from Connect to Environment.** The picker no longer lists the environments of remotes this window shares, since they're already reachable through their direct connections. Picking one used to add a second remote for the same host.

### How to test

1. Connect to a tunnel (or SSH) remote in the Agents window and share it as a GitHub environment from the Remotes editor.
2. Run **Connect to Environment**. The shared remote isn't listed.
3. In another window or on another computer signed in to the same account, run **Connect to Environment**. The remote is listed as `<remote name> (<application name>)`, and New Session shows the same name after connecting.

### Validation

- `scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/missionControlClientRegistration.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/missionControlEnvironmentActions.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/remoteGitHubEnvironmentSharingService.test.ts`: 574 passing, 1 pending.
- `scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/missionControlHost.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/missionControlClientRegistration.test.ts` (after the review fix): 43 passing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `node build/hygiene.ts`, `node build/lib/formatter.ts --verify` and `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed.
- I haven't tried it end to end with a real tunnel host.

Scenarios.Scenario: Share an SSH/tunnel/WSL remote as a GitHub environment, then stop or re-share it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sharing awaits account/session resolution, one registration RPC to the already-connected host, filesystem-root discovery, environment configuration, and initial registration/relay readiness. The diff adds a configured-entry lookup and optional display-name formatting, not another awaited operation. Unsharing follows the existing withdrawal path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve authentication-provider sessions, optionally creating a session for interactive sharing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One account-resolution flow per sharing action, with up to two getSessions calls when a default account exists; interactive creation only when needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical session-resolution flow preceded registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Account resolution must finish before registration can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing JSON-RPC extension registration request over the direct remote transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per selected address; its existing payload now optionally includes one name string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One request with accountId and credential; no name field.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover local roots, resolve configured directories, and read or initialize persisted compute identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Non-Windows root discovery returns '/' without I/O; Windows probes 26 drive letters and realpaths existing directories. Configuration resolves deduplicated roots and the home directory. Compute-identity I/O occurs when building a registration record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery, realpath, and identity-persistence work ran at the same frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Root resolution and cold identity persistence precede registration completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate the GitHub identity, register the environment, obtain signing keys when absent/stale, and establish the relay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One identity validation per live configure; a cold successful check-in sends one environment registration and one signing-key request before relay connection. Existing periodic heartbeat/token recovery and backoff remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same requests and relay setup ran; registration and heartbeat bodies already contained an environment name.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial sharing waits for configuration and relay readiness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One registration per selected remote. The new name lookup scans/normalizes the configured-entry collection once; the name is one ordinary remote display string. Host filesystem roots are deduplicated with the home directory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The sharing service uses one Sequencer for sharing and synchronization; the host registration and environment configuration each have their existing sequencers. Windows drive discovery retains its parallel batch of 26 probes; root resolution is parallel within one configuration. Different windows/hosts remain independently scheduled as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Display-name overrides use an observable owner or the existing storage getter. A new host registration computes its name once; subsequent registration calls retain the configured name. Initial compute identity uses persisted state, and signing keys retain their existing five-minute cache. No new cache or retry policy is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete registration call chain that RPC count, filesystem multiplicity, and network scheduling are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configured-entry counts and remote/network latency vary; no runtime timings were collected. The added local lookup and ordinary name string do not establish an actionable degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change passes naming metadata through existing work and retains only one additional configured-name string per host.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh shared-remote credentials after reconnection, authentication changes, or host restart
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing background synchronization resolves the account once, then awaits registration for each eligible stored share. Explicit sharing can wait behind this existing queue. The new helper obtains a name locally; an already-configured host ignores subsequent client-name differences by reusing its configured name.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve account sessions once per synchronization and register eligible direct connections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One account-resolution flow per synchronization when enabled with connections or stored shares; zero registration calls for warm _synced entries, otherwise one per eligible unsynchronized address.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same generation/handshake deduplication and serial registration loop ran without sending a client name.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background work is off the picker display path; its existing serial queue also orders explicit share/unshare actions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate refreshed credentials and perform existing conditional check-in, token refresh, signing-key retrieval, or relay recovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One identity validation for each issued live configure. Additional operations depend on existing credential, heartbeat, token, relay, and signing-key state rather than the number of display names or client renames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical renewal path and conditional boundary counts applied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each serial renewal waits for its host response; other addresses wait behind it as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S eligible stored shares among E configured entries; at most one registration per unsynchronized connected address per handshake/generation. The new helper adds an O(E) local lookup for each issued registration, not a boundary call per configured entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One renderer-wide synchronization Sequencer awaits addresses serially. RunOnceScheduler coalesces same-turn triggers. Each host serializes configuration, and _checkIn joins existing work for the same generation. No new cross-address burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing _synced map skips addresses already synchronized for their InitializeResult. Reconnects or generation invalidation allow renewal. Missing/offline connections are skipped; scheduling and failure retry conditions are unchanged. The configured host name remains stable across refreshes and is recomputed only for a new registration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged boundary frequency and global serialization from _synced, _queue, and the host configuration checks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large configured-entry collections add local lookup work, but registrations remain low-frequency connection/account events and no concrete user-visible regression is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Client renames do not force teardown/re-registration or defeat the existing synchronization cache.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, refresh, and close Connect to Environment while shared-remotes membership changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening still awaits inventory.initialize before showing cached inventory; refresh starts after the picker is shown. The diff reads the existing shared-environment-ID observable, filters locally, and subscribes until the picker resources are disposed. First use may instantiate the delayed sharing singleton, whose scheduled synchronization is not awaited by this command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the account and query the local agent host's Mission Control environment ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local-ID query per account-bearing initialization and another per inventory refresh; initialization callers share an in-flight promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initialization and refresh queries were made.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial initialization precedes picker display; refresh-time queries occur after display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the account's environment inventory through one SDK list operation, rather than one query per host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical list operation per explicit refresh, covering the inventory; filtering does not change request cardinality or add per-host reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The picker already performed this forced refresh and displayed its results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the picker is shown and blocks only completion of refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential cold activation of the existing sharing service's account resolution and stored-share renewal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only if the delayed singleton was not already instantiated. Initial synchronization resolves an account only when enabled and connections/stored shares exist, then follows the deduplicated serial per-address renewal path described above; zero per displayed inventory row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This command did not itself request the sharing singleton; existing sharing/remotes UI consumers could already have instantiated it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scheduled background work is not awaited before showing the picker. Existing consumers in the Agents UI already activate this service.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H discovered hosts, E configured remotes, and S share records. Filtering adds one Set.has per host; the existing shared-ID derivation can scan shares/configured entries. Sorting and connection-status mapping operate on the remaining hosts, not on all remote items as separate network requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A picker busy flag prevents overlapping refreshes from its button; inventory initialization coalesces in-flight initialization. The new observation does not issue requests. Cold sharing-singleton synchronization is scheduled/coalesced onto its own existing serial queue, independently of picker refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Inventory initialization shares an in-flight promise and restores cached hosts. Shared environmentIds is an existing derived observable with set-equality suppression, so unchanged membership does not notify the picker. API inventory has a 60-second cache, but this command's explicit refresh already bypassed it before the diff. Picker subscriptions are disposed on exit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that filtering itself is local, membership changes are equality-suppressed, and resources clean up the new autorun subscription.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold singleton activation depends on which UI/services have already been used; host/share collection sizes and authentication duration are unmeasured. No newly blocking request or realistic high-frequency workload was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The filter reduces rendered items, does not fan out inventory requests, and does not await sharing-service synchronization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select an unshared environment and establish its connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After selection, the existing service reuses a live/in-progress connection or awaits environment validation, connection credentials, remote relay establishment, and the protocol handshake. The diff only prevents selecting environments already represented by configured shared remotes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch selected-environment details, request connection credentials, establish the relay, and perform the remote handshake.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero new setup for a reusable live connection; otherwise one selected-environment detail operation and one successful credential-admission operation plus relay/handshake setup, subject to existing paced retries and deadlines.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operations ran for any selected environment, including shared remotes that are now excluded from the picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection completion waits for these existing operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check the local agent host's own environment ID before connecting a user-local environment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check for a new user-local connection attempt; none is added per picker row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical own-environment guard ran before connection setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes credential minting for a new connection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected environment ID, independent of total picker rows. Concurrent requests for the same ID join one pending connection operation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One connection attempt per selected environment ID; existing deadline, retry delays, cancellation, and account-scoped connection handling are unchanged. No new multi-host connection loop is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connected/connecting/reconnecting remote entries are reused. The pending-connect map coalesces requests by environment ID and removes completed entries. Unselected hosts do not initiate environment-detail or connect requests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the selected-ID call chain and the existing pending/reuse guards.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual network and handshake duration is not measured; no changed scheduling or call multiplicity exists on this selection path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change removes an opportunity for redundant connections rather than introducing additional setup work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the entire 14-file inventory and every diff page for the performance-review pass, then traced registration, credential renewal, picker initialization/refresh/lifetime, and selected-environment connection boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying historical performance fix was established. Static read-only review; no runtime profiling.
